extracted.intended_audience: general readers and speculative-fiction writers (particularly Black SFF authors) seeking information about FIYAH magazine
extracted.subtask_description: Information about FIYAH Literary Magazine's mission, formats, publication cadence, payment practices, diversity/inclusion initiatives, and recognition — useful for writers considering submission or researchers studying the magazine.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial mission / target contributors
rubrics_metrics.description: FIYAH's expressed goal was to create a publishing space for Black science fiction and fantasy (SFF) writers, who had been marginalized out of the mainstream SFF market.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The magazine seeks work by both native and diasporic Africans "that reject[s] regressive ideas of blackness, respectability politics, and stereotype." This frames submission suitability: pieces should center or responsibly represent Black perspectives and actively avoid stereotypical or 'respectability politics' approaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accepted content types
rubrics_metrics.description: Items published include prose stories, essays and poetry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FIYAH publishes multiple literary forms; submitters should target one of these formats. The magazine is electronic and quarterly, so editorial selection will be for those primary forms rather than other media.

rubrics_metrics.name: Themed-issue alignment
rubrics_metrics.description: Many of the issues are themed (e.g. "Hair", "Chains", "Haunting and Horrors", "Food and Cuisine", and "Palestinian Solidarity").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because issues are often built around a theme, submissions that engage a current or announced theme are more likely to fit an issue. Authors should check issue themes and tailor submissions when appropriate; non-theme-aligned work may be considered but thematic fit is relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author compensation / professional rate
rubrics_metrics.description: In 2020 FIYAH began paying $.08 per word, considered a "professional" rate by the Science Fiction and Fantasy Writers Association.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The magazine shifted from flat rates to per-word payment; the $.08/word rate is explicitly cited as professional. This is a production/payment standard for contributors and signals professionalism and market-level compensation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication schedule and format
rubrics_metrics.description: FIYAH is an American-based quarterly electronic magazine.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The quarterly cadence and electronic format set expectations for publication timing, editorial cycles, and when to expect issues (useful for planning submissions and rights/availability timing).

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion metric: Presence of Blackness Score Project
rubrics_metrics.description: In 2017 the magazine launched its Presence of Blackness Score Project to track the progress of short SFF markets in improving their accessibility to and publication of Black authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an explicit metric-oriented initiative: FIYAH evaluates and publicly tracks market-level accessibility and publication rates for Black authors. It signals editorial priority on measurable inclusion and may inform the magazine's own selection and advocacy practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognition of inclusion efforts: Ignyte Awards
rubrics_metrics.description: FIYAH created the Ignyte Awards to celebrate efforts towards inclusion and diversity within speculative fiction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Ignyte Awards function as a standard/recognition framework for work (individuals, projects, or organizations) that advance inclusion and diversity. Nomination/award criteria are oriented toward celebrating inclusive contributions in SFF.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality/reputation indicators (Locus recommendations; Hugos)
rubrics_metrics.description: By 2018, six of the 17 stories published that year were on Locus Magazine's recommended reading list; FIYAH has had multiple Hugo Award for Best Semiprozine nominations and won in 2021.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: High placement on Locus' recommended reading lists and nominations/wins for major genre awards are presented as markers of the magazine's quality. For authors, being published in FIYAH can be associated with visibility and critical recognition; for editors, these are outcome metrics of editorial selection quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternative publication pathways: contests and anthology collaborations
rubrics_metrics.description: FIYAH produced FIYAHCON and collaborated with Tor.com on the 'Breathe FIYAH' anthology and on the LeVar Burton Reads contest (three finalist short stories were selected for publication on Tor.com).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FIYAH facilitates publication via conventions, contests, and anthology collaborations; authors may gain entry via contests or special projects as well as regular submissions. Such collaborations also indicate opportunities for wider distribution and cross-publication.
